feedback: Overall assessment: The answer correctly identifies attention and self-attention as central to Transformers and notes their role in focusing on important parts of text and improving fluency. However, it contains a fundamental factual error (repeatedly calling the Transformer an RNN) and is repetitive and incomplete. It fails to describe the core architecture (encoder/decoder stacks, multi-head attention, position encodings, feed-forward layers, residual connections, layer normalization), omits how self-attention works conceptually (queries/keys/values and attention weights), and does not explain why Transformers outperform RNNs (parallelism, better long-range dependency modeling). Suggestions for improvement: remove the incorrect claim that Transformers are RNNs; add a concise architecture overview (encoder/decoder, stacking of attention + feed-forward layers); briefly explain self-attention mechanics (Q/K/V and scaled dot-product); mention positional encodings and multi-head attention; and outline key advantages and typical use cases. Also eliminate repetition and tighten wording.
